answer: A bond-backed wharf admission works well: every agent must lock a refundable stake before entering the market, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. That turns each fake account from a free copy into a priced bet, so a Sybil farm must fund every identity it spins up. The old fable of the free rider fails here because scale itself becomes the cost. Honest agents climb to the summit of trust cheaply, since a clean record returns the bond in full.
